description: `3 = 5` assigns to a bare number literal, not a place, raising the runtime's own `ol-not-a-place` (issue #94/#156). The parser structurally accepts a literal in target position precisely so this rule — not an internal-invariant throw — can explain the mistake (`checker-not-a-place.ts`'s doc comment; `spec/tooling.md:216-222`). `params.text` carries the FULL target surface text (`3`), matching the semantic-stage rule from issue #113. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
